newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt rises as funds influx continues.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt rises as funds influx continues.

text.p: Emerging markets bonds rose strongly Friday as a more-positive outlook on U.S. interest rates buoyed investment flows to the sector, traders and analysts said.

Spreads over Treasuries narrowed about 20 basis points overall by midafternoon, traders said. A late rally in the U.S. Treasury market -- upon the announcement of a balanced budget deal -- cut into the spread reduction somewhat.
"Obviously, our market's done quite well," one trader said. "All the high yield markets have seen money come back into them."

The April U.S. employment report dominated Friday's economic news, traders said. It showed payrolls grew 142,000 after a revised 139,000 in March, average hourly earnings declined 0.1 percent after rising 0.4 percent the month before and the unemployment rate dipped to 4.9 percent from 5.2 percent.
Even with the low jobless rate, the below-forecast payrolls figure and decline in earnings were "very good news," a Brady trader said.
Trading volume generally remained thin Friday because many players took leave after the May Day holiday, traders said.
Major latins racked up impressive gains. Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR jumped 1-1/8 to 77-3/8 bid, and Mexico pars MX625L19=RR were up 7/8 at 73-5/8.
Argentine paper also was well-bid in somewhat heavier trade, traders, said.
"The Argie bonds have been trading the best. They're the ones I feel a little more bullish on, and I've seen people focusing there," one trader said.
Late Friday, Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR were up 1/4 at 92-1/2 bid, and Argentina discounts AR425C23=RR had risen 5/8 to 84 bid.
Many issues in the broader market performed equally well.

Funds from a variety of sources flowed into emerging bonds over the past two weeks, suggesting a more-bullish outlook had established a foothold, said Raul Elizalde, senior quantitative analyst at ING Barings.
"The flows have increased to emerging markets and to high yield, and that seems to indicate that at least for right now, we have pretty bullish sentiment. It's not just a pop," Elizalde said.
An improved outlook for U.S. interest rates allowed portfolio cash that had been on hold to flow back into the market, he said.
"When rates go down considerably, you want to go for the riskier stuff," Elizalde said.
